notes.md: - **[25 Oct 2026] Lionel Messi - Princess of Asturias Award for Sports-2026**: **23 October 2026**, **Oviedo, Spain**; **first footballer** to win it individually; presented by **Princess Leonor**; awards instituted **1981**, **eight categories**; Messi (club **Inter Miami**) led Argentina to the **2022 FIFA World Cup (Qatar)**; record **eight Ballon d'Or** awards.

- **[24–26 Oct 2026] International Criminal Court (ICC) and its officials receive the Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought 2026**: by the **European Parliament** - the **EU's highest human rights honour** (EP President **Roberta Metsola**); given amid US President **Donald Trump's sanctions** on the ICC; established **1988** for **Andrei Sakharov (Nobel Peace 1975)**; first awarded jointly in **1988** to **Nelson Mandela** and **Anatoly Marchenko**; carries **EUR 50,000** and citation; ICC under the **Rome Statute 1998**, operational since **1 July 2002**, HQ **The Hague**; ICC President **Tomoko Akane of Japan**; **India and the US are not parties**.

- Israel's highest civilian honour is the **Presidential Medal of Distinction**.
- **UAE**: capital **Abu Dhabi**, currency **Dirham**, est. **2 Dec 1971**; **flydubai** - Dubai-based, operations since **2009**.
- **Shashi Tharoor**: France's **Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur** (announced Aug 2022).
- **Literature**: **Herta Müller (2009)**; J.M. Coetzee (2003); Jon Fosse (2023).
- **USA** has the most laureates (India, China, Iran only a handful).
- **68th** awards, theme "**A World for All**"; announced **31 August 2026** (Ramon Magsaysay's birth anniversary); to be presented **15 November 2026**, Manila.

- Founded **2007** by **Safeena Husain**; works in **Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh** (in all **12 states**, **30,000+ villages**); volunteers called "**Team Balika**"; **1.9 million+** (about 2 million) girls back to school.
- Other **TIME Women of the Year 2026**: **Reshma Kewalramani, Reshma Saujani, Chloé Zhao, Lucy Liu, Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone**.

- Other Padma Shri 2026 (Art): **R. Madhavan** (Maharashtra), **Prosenjit Chatterjee** (West Bengal), **Satish Shah** (posthumous, Maharashtra), **Gayatri and Ranjani Balasubramanian** (duo, Tamil Nadu).
- Instituted **1954**; announced on **Republic Day** (eve, 25 January) through a **Ministry of Home Affairs notification**; **suspended 1977–80 and 1992–95**.
- **Article 18(1)**: no titles except **military and academic distinctions**; **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)**: Padma awards are **not titles under Article 18**; not to be used as prefix or suffix.
- Count asked: **2009 – 93 Padma Shri**.

- Instituted **1991** by the **K.K. Birla Foundation** (first 1992, Harivansh Rai Bachchan); for a work published in the **last 10 years**; **₹15 lakh**. **2016: Mahabaleshwar Sail** (Konkani) for **Hawthan**. **35th (2025): Ramkumar Mukhopadhyay** – Bengali novel **Hara Parbati Katha**.

- **Booker Prize:** for the best sustained work of **fiction written in English**, published in the UK/Ireland; by the **Booker Prize Foundation**; **£50,000** (plus **£2,500** to each of the **six** shortlisted authors); presented by **David Szalay**, the **2025 winner** (**Flesh**).

- **[04–05 Nov 2026] ₹250 commemorative coin on the 250th birth anniversary of Muthuswami Dikshitar** – released by **FM Nirmala Sitharaman** in **Varanasi**; highlighted his Kashi links and compositions to Goddesses **Annapurna and Vishalakshi**; **Dikshitar (1775–1835)**, born **Tiruvarur**; mudra/signature "**Guruguha**"; a **veena** player; composed mostly in **Sanskrit**; famous works '**Annapurne Visalakshi**', '**Sri Viswanatham Bhajeham**'; one of the **Carnatic Trinity** with **Tyagaraja (1767–1847**, Pancharatna Kritis) and **Syama Sastri (1762–1827**, mudra "Syama Krishna").
- **Bhupen Hazarika**: Phalke **1992**; Padma Vibhushan **2012**.
- **Article 343** - Hindi in **Devanagari** script is the official language of the Union.
- Mridangam schools: **Thanjavur** and **Pudukkottai**; Carnatic Trinity - **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri**.

- India's **97 para-athletes** won the 114 medals – **65 in para athletics**; **Nishad Kumar** – two golds (para athletics); **Mona Agarwal** – two golds (**para shooting**); **PM Modi felicitated** the contingent (**7 Nov 2026**).
- India's earlier best: Hangzhou 2022 (held 2023) – 111. The Games evolved from the **FESPIC Games (1975)**. **IPC** est. **1989**, HQ **Bonn**.

- **Inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026**, **Ahmedabad** (13 men's and 10 women's teams): India won both titles – women (capt. **Nidhi Sharma**) beat **Uganda 35–15**, men (capt. **Surjeet Singh**) beat Sri Lanka 54–20.

- **Hylo Open 2026** (Super 500), **Saarbrücken, Germany** (formerly the **BMW Badminton Cup**, held since **1988**): **P.V. Sindhu** (women's singles, beat **Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt**, Denmark) and **Lakshya Sen** (men's, beat Jonatan Christie).

- Co-hosted by **India and Sri Lanka** (30 Sep – 2 Nov 2025); final at **DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai** (**2 November 2025**): **India** beat **South Africa** by 52 runs – India's **maiden title** (India had lost the 2005 and 2017 finals; South Africa's first final; SA captain **Laura Wolvaardt** scored a century in the final).

- **CWG 2030 Ahmedabad** (centenary; first Games **1930, Hamilton**, Canada – not 1934): awarded at the Commonwealth Sport **General Assembly, Glasgow, 26 November 2025** (over **Abuja**, Nigeria); India's **second** CWG after **Delhi 2010** – **Asia's first repeat host**; **Rahul Dravid and Saina Nehwal** nominated as athlete representatives on the Organising Committee Board (2 Nov 2026); OC to follow the **2006 Melbourne** model (not-for-profit corporate entity).
- The CWG is held every **4 years**; the Commonwealth has **56** members.

- The **first T20 World Cup co-hosted by two countries** (India and Sri Lanka); India the **first to host as defending champion**.
- **Divya Deshmukh:** India's **4th woman GM** (88th GM), earned by winning the Women's World Cup 2025.

- **[07 Nov 2026] 150 years of Vande Mataram:** the year-long **150th-year celebration (7 Nov 2025 – 7 Nov 2026)**, which PM Modi marked in the **127th Mann Ki Baat (26 Oct 2025)**, ended – the **Ministry of Railways** closed its celebration; composed by **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (Chattopadhyay)** in **Sanskrit** (GoI wording; also described as Sanskritised Bengali); first published in the journal **Bangadarshan (7 Nov 1875)**, later in the novel **Anandamath (1882)**; meaning "**I bow to thee, Mother**"; first sung by **Tagore** at the **1896 Calcutta INC session**; first a political slogan on **7 August 1905** – the rallying cry of the **Swadeshi Movement (1905–1911)**; its first two stanzas were designated **National Song** by **Dr Rajendra Prasad** in the Constituent Assembly on **24 January 1950** (not 26 January) – equal status with Jana Gana Mana.
- **1937 CWC**: only the first two stanzas at national gatherings.

- **Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath** (near Varanasi, UP) inscribed at the **48th World Heritage Committee, Busan, South Korea (July 2026)**; components include the **Chaukhandi Stupa** and archaeological remains; criteria **(iii) and (vi)**.
- India now **45 WHS** – **6th globally, 2nd in Asia-Pacific**; **UP's 4th** (others: **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri**); on the tentative list since **3 July 1998** (about 28 years).
- One nomination per year; nodal **ASI**.

- Ministry of Culture **final notification** – **Gollalagudi Temple** near **Ramappa Temple, Palampet, Mulugu** district, **Telangana**; ~**0.25 acres** protected (Survey No. 417/3); draft notification on 6 March under **Section 4(1), AMASR Act, 1958**.
- **Netaji** escaped house arrest in **1941**.
- **2018 Guillermo Cano Prize** – **Mahmoud Abu Zeid ("Shawkan")**, Egyptian photojournalist (given **2 May**).
- Other 2026: **Shantanu Moitra** – Lata Mangeshkar Alankaran Samman.

fix.s: Who is the CEO of NITI Aayog (from 17 August 2026)?
fix.x: Anurag Jain became the regular CEO of NITI Aayog from 17 August 2026. Nidhi Chhibber had held additional charge after B.V.R. Subrahmanyam; Amitabh Kant was an earlier CEO.

fix.s: During which periods were the Padma Awards suspended?
fix.x: The Padma Awards were suspended twice: from 1977 to 1980 and from 1992 to 1995 (the second ended with the Balaji Raghavan judgment, 1996).
